article_title: StanBKT: Rethinking Parameter Estimation in Bayesian Knowledge Tracing
citation: Siddhartha Pradhan, Yanping Pei, Morgan Lee, Puyuan Zhang, Erin Ottmar, and Adam C. Sales. (2026). StanBKT: Rethinking Parameter Estimation in Bayesian Knowledge Tracing. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23048
title: Three pooling formulations for BKT: standard, multi (group-specific), and hierarchical (partial pooling)
description: StanBKT organizes BKT formulations into three pooling types. Standard BKT shares a single parameter set across all students (full pooling, assuming homogeneous learning and response behavior). Multi BKT estimates a separate parameter set for each predefined group such as classrooms, treatment conditions, or individual students, enabling direct comparison across groups. Hierarchical BKT introduces partial pooling through hierarchical priors, decomposing each parameter into a global component and group-level deviations with a learned variance controlling shrinkage. The article states this formulation "stabilizes and regularizes estimates in sparse data contexts while preserving systematic differences across groups."
requirements: Grouped and hierarchical variants require a group identifier column in the interaction data
constraints: Standard BKT assumes homogeneous learning and response behavior across students and items
target_learners: students grouped by classroom, treatment condition, cohort, or individual
target_learning_goals: comparing learning dynamics across experimental conditions and stabilizing estimates in sparse-data settings
examples: The perceptual cue reanalysis used Multi BKT with condition-specific parameters across the nine spacing-by-color conditions, fit via MCMC
key_sources: Siddhartha Pradhan, Yanping Pei, Morgan Lee, Puyuan Zhang, Erin Ottmar, and Adam C. Sales. (2026). StanBKT: Rethinking Parameter Estimation in Bayesian Knowledge Tracing. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23048
grain_size: model-specification pattern for student modeling studies

article_title: AI Adaptivity in a Mixed-Reality System Improves Learning
citation: Yannier, N., Hudson, S. E., Chang, H., & Koedinger, K. R. (2024). AI Adaptivity in a Mixed-Reality System Improves Learning. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 34, 1541–1558. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-023-00388-5
title: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing for task-loop adaptivity in mixed-reality learning
description: The article applies Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, which "models student knowledge growth as a latent variable using a two-state Hidden Markov Model", to select tasks in an Intelligent Science Station. Each knowledge component has four parameters (p(L0), p(T), p(S), p(G)), and mastery is declared when prediction and explanation Ln scores both exceed 0.95. Task selection implements a "gentle slope" of improvement, picking the unmastered category closest to mastery.
requirements: A specialized AI computer vision algorithm that assesses children's physical experimentation so mastery can be updated per task
constraints: Parameter values were estimated from prior log data and pilot testing; the authors note future work could add student-specific parameter adjustments
target_learning_goals: physics principles of stability and balance (height, base-width, symmetry, center of mass)
key_sources: Yannier, N., Hudson, S. E., Chang, H., & Koedinger, K. R. (2024). AI Adaptivity in a Mixed-Reality System Improves Learning. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 34, 1541–1558. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-023-00388-5
